dossier.purpose: Grafana is a Go backend plus TypeScript/React web application that queries external data sources and renders dashboards and Explore views. It also evaluates alert rules and sends notifications (README.md:4,8; AGENTS.md:16). It keeps only its own state (users, dashboards, data-source config) in SQLite by default, with MySQL and PostgreSQL supported (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/_index.md:138-146). The metric, log and trace stores it queries are separate software with their own sizing (installation/_index.md:55). Facts per stated need, for v13.2.3: (1) Local OTLP ingestion point and privacy filter for Claude Code/Codex telemetry: none. No OTLP receiver or telemetry-redaction pipeline exists in pkg/, apps/, conf/, public/app or docs/sources. OTLP code is exporter-only for Grafana's own traces (pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:176-196; tracing_file.go:29-37). (2) Store for native usage metrics received over OTLP: none; Grafana queries external stores (docs/sources/datasources/_index.md:103). (3) Store for events/logs received over OTLP: none. The Faro-style /log-grafana-javascript-agent endpoint only writes to the Grafana server log and is off by default (pkg/api/frontend_logging.go:33-93; pkg/setting/setting_grafana_javascript_agent.go:26). (4) Local dashboards and exploration over metrics/log stores: yes (public/app/features/dashboard-scene, public/app/features/explore). The Prometheus, Loki, Tempo etc. data-source plugins are not in this source tree; they are catalog plugins downloaded from grafana.com and bundled or preinstalled (scripts/catalog-plugins-defaults:3-15; pkg/setting/setting_plugins.go:35-55). (5) Store for traces, datasets and experiments to replay a fixed workload against model routes: none found. Grep for gen_ai / AI observability / prompt replay / eval dataset hits only nav entries for external apps grafana-sigil-app and grafana-agento11y-app (pkg/services/navtree/navtreeimpl/applinks.go:594-595). (6) Local model server on a GPU host: none. There is no ollama/vllm/llama.cpp code or config. The only model-related code is optional cloud embedding providers vertex/bedrock/azure (pkg/storage/unified/search/embed/embedder/provider/provider.go:42-53). Grafana Assistant on-prem needs a Grafana Cloud stack (docs/sources/administration/assistant/_index.md:16-36).

claims.claim: Tagline: 'The open-source platform for monitoring and observability'.
'Grafana allows you to query, visualize, alert on and understand your metrics no matter where they are stored.' It describes querying stores, not ingesting or storing telemetry.
Visualizations: fast client-side graphs; panel plugins visualize metrics and logs.
Dynamic dashboards: reusable dashboards with template variables shown as dropdowns.
Explore Metrics: ad-hoc queries, dynamic drilldown, split view to compare time ranges, queries and data sources.
Explore Logs: switch from metrics to logs with preserved label filters; search or live-stream logs.
Alerting: visually defined alert rules, continuously evaluated, with notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, VictorOps, OpsGenie.
Mixed data sources: choose a data source per query in the same graph, including custom data sources.
Install: the README gives no commands, only links to https://grafana.com/get and the installation guides.
A hosted demo exists at play.grafana.org; documentation lives at grafana.com/docs.
License: AGPL-3.0-only, with Apache-2.0 exceptions listed in LICENSING.md.
Silence: the 51-line README says nothing about OTLP ingestion, telemetry/phone-home, MCP, Claude Code/Codex, local model serving, GPU use or platform support.

install.method: APT repository (Debian/Ubuntu, Linux); OSS package is 'grafana', Enterprise package is 'grafana-enterprise'
install.command: sudo apt-get install -y apt-transport-https wget gnupg; sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings; sudo wget -O /etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.asc https://apt.grafana.com/gpg-full.key; sudo chmod 644 /etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.asc; echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.asc] https://apt.grafana.com stable main" | sudo tee -a /etc/apt/sources.list.d/grafana.list; sudo apt-get update; sudo apt-get install grafana

wget -q -O gpg.key https://rpm.grafana.com/gpg.key; sudo rpm --import gpg.key; (create /etc/yum.repos.d/grafana.repo with [grafana] baseurl=https://rpm.grafana.com repo_gpgcheck=1 gpgcheck=1 gpgkey=https://rpm.grafana.com/gpg.key); sudo dnf install grafana

install.method: Docker image (Linux/macOS). The documented command uses grafana/grafana-enterprise; the OSS image is grafana/grafana, and grafana/grafana-oss is no longer updated from 12.4.0.

install.command: brew update; brew install grafana; brew services start grafana

install.method: Standalone tar.gz binary (Linux/macOS). The download snippet lives on https://grafana.com/grafana/download, not in this repo; after untarring, start the server:

install.command: git clone https://github.com/grafana/grafana.git; corepack enable; corepack install; yarn install --immutable; yarn start (frontend, watch); make run (backend on http://localhost:3000, login admin/admin)

platforms.linux_x86_64: yes: linux-amd64 is in the release build matrix for tar.gz, deb, rpm and Docker (.github/workflows/release-build.yml:219-221,287-289,381-384,491-506). Debian/Ubuntu, RHEL/Fedora and SUSE are the documented Linux installs (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/_index.md:32-38).
platforms.wsl2: unknown: no install doc targets WSL2, and the docs call other operating systems 'not recommended or supported' (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/_index.md:40-42). WSL is mentioned only for developing on Windows 10 (contribute/developer-guide.md:26) and for running migration snippets (docs/sources/administration/migration-guide/manually-migrate-to-grafana-cloud.md:50). A WSL2 distro would use the Linux packages, but that is not documented.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes: the macOS guide covers Homebrew on Apple Silicon (/opt/homebrew) and standalone macOS binaries (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/mac/index.md:38-39,63-81). The release workflow builds and publishes a darwin-arm64 tar.gz (.github/workflows/release-build.yml:250-252,318-320,682).
platforms.gpu: no: Grafana does not use a GPU. The only GPU mention in docs/sources is the image renderer's default '--disable-gpu' Chromium flag (docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md:3005); a grep for GPU/CUDA/nvidia over docs/sources found nothing else.

integrations.cli: yes: one 'grafana' binary with 'server' and 'cli' subcommands (pkg/cmd/grafana/main.go:59-72). 'grafana cli plugins' has install, list-remote, list-versions, update, update-all, ls and uninstall. 'grafana cli admin' has reset-admin-password, data-migration, secrets-migration, secrets-consolidation, flush-rbac-seed-assignment, db-migrate and resource-db-migrate (pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/commands/commands.go:91-259). The deb package also installs grafana-server and grafana-cli wrappers in /usr/sbin (scripts/build-deb.sh:75-82). Homebrew CLI usage is documented (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/mac/index.md:47-61).
integrations.mcp: none found in this repo: a grep for MCP / model context protocol across code and docs hits only the Grafana Assistant docs. Those mention 'MCP server integrations' for the separate grafana-assistant-app plugin, whose backend runs in a Grafana Cloud stack (docs/sources/administration/assistant/_index.md:16,24-36,47; docs/sources/administration/roles-and-permissions/access-control/plugin-role-definitions/index.md:204).
integrations.sdk_or_api: HTTP API: every instance exposes one, documented with OpenAPI v2/v3 specs (public/api-merged.json, public/openapi3.json) and a Swagger UI served by the server. Auth is basic auth or a service-account token (docs/sources/developer-resources/api-reference/http-api/_index.md:26,41-52). A newer Kubernetes-style /apis API is being introduced while legacy /api is deprecated (http-api/_index.md:30-37; pkg/registry/apis/*/register.go). SDKs: Go github.com/grafana/grafana-plugin-sdk-go and grafana-app-sdk (go.mod:105,112); npm @grafana/data, ui, runtime and schema, which are Apache-2.0 (LICENSING.md:12-15; .github/workflows/release-npm.yml:44-62).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found as a product integration: a grep for Claude Code / Codex / Anthropic API found only a CODEOWNERS comment (.github/CODEOWNERS:835). Contributor-facing agent files exist: AGENTS.md:5 ('guidance to AI agents when working with code in the Grafana repository'), CLAUDE.md:1 (imports @AGENTS.md), .claude/skills/add-e2e-selectors/SKILL.md and .claude/skills/panel-testing-strategy/SKILL.md.

readme.telemetry_and_network:
Phones home by default; each item can be disabled in config.
(1) Anonymous usage report. POST to https://stats.grafana.org/grafana-usage-report every 24 h with version, OS, arch, edition, packaging, a random anonymous UUID and aggregate counters. On unless [analytics] reporting_enabled=false (pkg/infra/usagestats/service/usage_stats.go:29,41-48,130-184,186-211; pkg/infra/usagestats/service/service.go:70; pkg/setting/setting.go:1680; conf/defaults.ini:383-388; docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md:609-616).
(2) Version check. GET https://grafana.com/api/grafana/versions/stable at startup and every 24 h, on unless [analytics] check_for_updates=false (pkg/services/updatemanager/grafana.go:23,60-76,95; pkg/setting/setting.go:1661; conf/defaults.ini:393-398). Plugin update check against <grafana_com.api_url>/plugins/versioncheck every 10 min, on unless check_for_plugin_updates=false (pkg/services/updatemanager/plugins.go:71,106; pkg/setting/setting.go:1662).
(3) Plugin catalog. A background service preinstalls 18 default catalog plugins from grafana.com at startup and auto-updates unpinned ones: Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Elasticsearch, Jaeger, Zipkin, InfluxDB, MySQL, Postgres, MSSQL, OpenTSDB, Stackdriver, Pyroscope, the four drilldown apps and the advisor app. Enterprise builds add grafana-assistant-app. Async failures are logged and skipped, while preinstall_sync failures halt startup (pkg/setting/setting_plugins.go:35-55,157-171,191,201; pkg/services/pluginsintegration/plugininstaller/service.go:84-147,150-168; conf/defaults.ini:2193-2228). Disable with [plugins] preinstall_disabled=true or preinstall_auto_update=false. Plugin-signature public keys are fetched from <api_url>/plugins/ci/keys unless public_key_retrieval_disabled=true (pkg/services/pluginsintegration/keyretriever/dynamic/dynamic_retriever.go:119; conf/defaults.ini:2206-2210).
(4) News feed. The browser fetches https://grafana.com/blog/news.xml when [news] news_feed_enabled=true, the default (public/app/plugins/panel/news/constants.ts:1; conf/defaults.ini:1994-1996; pkg/setting/setting.go:1724).
(5) Default CSP template lists grafana.com in connect-src, but CSP is off by default (conf/defaults.ini:542-547).
Off by default or optional: Google Analytics, Rudderstack, Application Insights and PostHog (conf/defaults.ini:407-454). The Faro-compatible /log-grafana-javascript-agent endpoint is disabled by default and, when enabled, only writes to the server log (pkg/setting/setting_grafana_javascript_agent.go:26; pkg/api/frontend_logging.go:33-93,101-127). OTLP/gRPC or Jaeger export of Grafana's own traces is off with an empty address, and there is a bounded OTLP/JSON local-file exporter (conf/defaults.ini:2094-2118; pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:176-224; pkg/infra/tracing/tracing_file.go:20-37). The feature-flag provider is 'static' (conf/defaults.ini:2365-2368).
Grafana's own Prometheus metrics at /metrics are enabled by default, with optional basic auth (conf/defaults.ini:2013-2028; docs/sources/setup-grafana/set-up-grafana-monitoring.md:59-82).
Accounts and services: no account is needed for the OSS server. SQLite is the default DB (conf/defaults.ini:223-228). The default login is admin/admin (conf/defaults.ini:471-474). Data sources need their own backends (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/_index.md:55). Grafana Assistant on-prem requires a Grafana Cloud stack that hosts its backend and billing (docs/sources/administration/assistant/_index.md:16,24-36).
Build-time network: packaging downloads catalog plugin zips from https://grafana.com/api/plugins (scripts/download-catalog-plugins.sh:6,146-157; Makefile:391-411).

entry_points.what: Unified 'grafana' binary; registers the 'server' and 'cli' subcommands (main.go:59-72). Built by Makefile:40-47 into bin/<os>/<arch>/grafana.
'grafana server' command (cli.go:13-23) delegating to pkg/server/bootstrap, plus a 'target' subcommand for running individual modules.
'grafana cli plugins ...' and 'grafana cli admin ...' command sets (commands.go:91-259).
Documents the server package and Wire DI sets (bootstrap/wire, oss/enterprise build tags); the service graph is built in pkg/server (wire.go, initialize_oss.go).
Packaging entry for .deb: installs /usr/sbin/grafana plus grafana-server/grafana-cli wrappers (packaging/wrappers/*) and the grafana-server systemd unit (build-deb.sh:75-110).

Image build with six variants (alpine, ubuntu, distroless, each full or slim). Alpine/ubuntu use packaging/docker/run.sh (Dockerfile:280-285); distroless runs 'grafana server' directly (Dockerfile:399-400); EXPOSE 3000.
Frontend entry scripts: 'yarn build' (webpack prod, line 12), 'yarn start' (dev watch, line 61), 'yarn test' (Jest, line 35), 'yarn e2e:playwright' (line 24).
Default configuration (overrides in conf/custom.ini or GF_* env vars) (AGENTS.md:144).

code.architecture:
Monolithic Go server serving a React single-page app.
Backend (pkg/): pkg/cmd/* entry points; pkg/server (+bootstrap) builds the service graph with Google Wire DI under oss/enterprise/pro build tags (pkg/server/doc.go:1-25; Makefile:263-275; AGENTS.md:143). pkg/api holds HTTP routes (e.g. api.go:546 for /api/live/push). pkg/services/* holds domain services: ngalert alerting with an Alertmanager fork (go.mod:727), live, updatemanager, pluginsintegration, navtree, featuremgmt and others. pkg/registry/apis, pkg/services/apiserver and apps/* form a Kubernetes-style /apis API built on the Grafana App SDK (dashboard, folder, iam, alerting rules/notifications, provisioning, secret...). pkg/storage/unified is a resource store with search and optional cloud-embedder vector search. pkg/plugins plus pluginsintegration load and install plugins; backend plugins use gRPC/protobuf (AGENTS.md:109). pkg/tsdb holds the only in-tree data-source backends: azuremonitor, cloudwatch, grafana-testdata-datasource, grafanads, graphite. pkg/infra covers log, metrics, tracing (exporter-only), usagestats and db. pkg/setting plus conf/defaults.ini handle configuration.
Frontend: public/app/core, public/app/features (dashboard-scene, explore, variables, alerting, plugins...), 30 built-in panel plugins (public/app/plugins/panel/*/plugin.json) and 8 in-tree data sources (alertmanager, azuremonitor, cloudwatch, dashboard, grafana, grafana-testdata-datasource, graphite, mixed). Shared npm packages live in packages/* and CUE kinds in kinds/.
Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Elasticsearch, Jaeger, Zipkin, InfluxDB, MySQL/Postgres/MSSQL, OpenTSDB, Stackdriver and Pyroscope are external catalog plugins. They are fetched at packaging time into data/plugins-bundled (scripts/catalog-plugins-defaults:3-15; scripts/download-catalog-plugins.sh) and preinstalled at runtime (pkg/setting/setting_plugins.go:35-55).
Grafana Live (pkg/services/live) is an in-memory pub/sub with optional Redis HA. Its HTTP push accepts InfluxDB line protocol only (pkg/services/live/pushhttp/push.go:48-100; pkg/services/live/convert/convert.go:30-45; docs/sources/setup-grafana/set-up-grafana-live.md:58,238).
code.packaging_and_release:
Artifacts (release-build.yml:22-27): tar.gz for linux amd64/arm64/s390x/armv6/armv7, linux riscv64 (allowed to fail, 'not an officially supported architecture'), windows amd64/arm64 and darwin amd64/arm64 (release-build.yml:273-320; Makefile:413-425). .deb for all Linux targets and .rpm for amd64/arm64/s390x/riscv64 (release-build.yml:368-406; Makefile:427-453). Docker images alpine/ubuntu/distroless, each full and slim, for amd64/arm64/s390x/armv7 (build-docker-variants.yml:63-100; release-build.yml:491-558). Windows zip and MSI (release-build.yml:582-663). Docker Hub repos are grafana/grafana (OSS) and grafana/grafana-enterprise; grafana/grafana-oss is no longer updated from 12.4.0 (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/docker/index.md:14-17,27-28).
Triggers: weekday-night schedule, pushes to main and release-*.*.*, manual (release-build.yml:2-17). Jobs run only for grafana/grafana main or the private security mirror's '#patched' branches, and the same workflow is dispatched in the private grafana-enterprise repo (release-build.yml:37-41,91-185).
Checksums: each artifact gets a bare sha256 '.sha256' sidecar (release-build.yml:334-340,431-437,632-638; build-docker-variants.yml:141-147). Upload goes to the GCS bucket 'grafana-prerelease' via publish-artifact.yml (release-build.yml:665-694; publish-artifact.yml:53-88). The release tag and GitHub release are created by release-comms.yml:133-163. An SPDX SBOM from Socket is attached (sbom-on-release.yml:69-85; release-comms.yml:165-180). deb/rpm from dl.grafana.com are attached after their sha256 is verified against the grafana.com packages API (release-comms.yml:182-252).
Signatures/attestations: no cosign/sigstore/SLSA/provenance steps anywhere under .github (grep). RPM signing ('rpm --addsign') and signed apt/rpm repo scripts exist (scripts/build/sign_packages.sh:17-25; scripts/build/update_repo/*). Docs say RPMs are signed and give GPG key URLs (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/redhat-rhel-fedora/index.md:81; debian/index.md:52-58). The signing itself runs outside the public workflows. npm @grafana/* packages publish through npm Trusted Publishing with OIDC (release-npm.yml:42-62). Reproducibility knobs: -trimpath, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and docker rewrite-timestamp (Makefile:24,34,469).
code.tests_and_ci:
Frameworks: Go 'go test' with testcontainers (pr-test-integration.yml:34-39); Jest 29.7 + React Testing Library + msw (package.json:116,205,222); Playwright 1.56.1 e2e (package.json:106); Vitest for rspack tests (package.json:44,250); Storybook tests (package.json:40). Approximate test-file counts from globs: 1,853 *_test.go under pkg/, 188 under apps/, 1,962 *.test.ts(x) under public/, 433 under packages/, and 212 Playwright *.spec.ts under e2e-playwright/.
CI: about 94 workflow YAMLs in .github/workflows plus 15 composite actions in .github/actions.
Workflows I read: backend-unit-tests.yml (8 shards of 'go test -vet=off -short -timeout=30m', CGO_ENABLED=0); pr-test-integration.yml (TestIntegration on SQLite in 4 shards and MySQL in 16 shards; later jobs not read); pr-frontend-unit-tests.yml (Jest in 16 shards); pr-e2e-tests.yml (builds backend and frontend, then Playwright); go-lint.yml (gofmt + golangci-lint v2.12.2); frontend-lint.yml (prettier, eslint, typecheck); govulncheck.yml (every Go module); trufflehog.yml (verified secrets); release-verify.yml (boots the built tar.gz and runs the Playwright acceptance suite).
Others exist by name only (not opened): pr-test-docker, pr-test-integration-pgvector, proto-breaking-changes, pr-k8s-codegen-check, swagger-gen, i18n-verify, documentation-ci, actionlint, shellcheck.
Caveat: for pushes to main/release branches and non-fork PRs, unit and lint jobs run against a checkout overlaying the private grafana-enterprise repo. The OSS-only jobs run only for fork PRs (backend-unit-tests.yml:38-42,72-125; frontend-lint.yml:40-47,60-87).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:8: 'query, visualize, alert on and understand your metrics no matter where they are stored'
claim_checks.evidence: True as a query/visualize layer: a data source is 'a connection to a storage backend' that Grafana queries (docs/sources/datasources/_index.md:103). Grafana has no metric store of its own. The in-tree data-source backends are only Graphite, CloudWatch, Azure Monitor and TestData (pkg/tsdb/{graphite,cloudwatch,azuremonitor,grafana-testdata-datasource}), plus the Grafana/Mixed/Dashboard/Alertmanager data sources (public/app/plugins/datasource/*/plugin.json). Prometheus, Loki, Tempo, Elasticsearch, Jaeger, Zipkin, InfluxDB, MySQL, Postgres, MSSQL, OpenTSDB, Stackdriver and Pyroscope are external catalog plugins (scripts/catalog-plugins-defaults:3-15), so reach depends on code not in this tree.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:4/8: an observability platform. The README never claims OTLP ingestion or storage; checked whether the code provides an OTLP receiver, telemetry store or privacy filter.
claim_checks.evidence: None found. Greps for otlp, receiver and '/v1/(traces|metrics|logs)' over pkg/, apps/, conf/, public/app and docs/sources show only: exporters for Grafana's own traces (pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:176-196; conf/defaults.ini:2100-2118), an OTLP/JSON file exporter (pkg/infra/tracing/tracing_file.go:29-37), a 'download trace as OTLP JSON' inspector helper (public/app/features/inspector/utils/download.ts:110-132), and go.opentelemetry.io/collector/pdata used only as a data-model library (go.mod:186). The only push intake is Grafana Live /api/live/push/:streamId (pkg/api/api.go:546), which converts InfluxDB line protocol into in-memory pub/sub frames (pkg/services/live/pushhttp/push.go:48-100; convert/convert.go:30-45). The Faro-style endpoint only logs and is off by default (pkg/api/frontend_logging.go:33-93; pkg/setting/setting_grafana_javascript_agent.go:26). No redaction pipeline for ingested telemetry exists.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:10-13: visualizations, dynamic dashboards with template variables, Explore Metrics, Explore Logs
claim_checks.evidence: Dashboards (public/app/features/dashboard-scene/scene/DashboardScene.tsx), Explore (public/app/features/explore/Explore.tsx), template variables (public/app/features/variables/**) and 30 built-in panel plugins (public/app/plugins/panel/*/plugin.json) are in-tree. The Metrics/Logs/Traces/Profiles drilldown apps are separate catalog apps preinstalled at startup and not in this tree (pkg/setting/setting_plugins.go:37-40; pkg/services/navtree/navtreeimpl/applinks.go:602-605).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:14: alert rules with notifications to Slack, PagerDuty, VictorOps, OpsGenie
claim_checks.evidence: The alerting engine and notifier plumbing are in-tree (pkg/services/ngalert/ngalert.go; pkg/services/ngalert/notifier/*; Alertmanager fork go.mod:727). Integration implementations come from the external module github.com/grafana/alerting (go.mod:94), and integration_schemas.go contains none of those names. Docs list VictorOps among contact points (docs/sources/alerting/configure-notifications/manage-contact-points/_index.md:188) and have pages for Slack, PagerDuty and Opsgenie (.../integrations/configure-slack.md, pager-duty.md, configure-opsgenie.md).

The Grafana version check does GET https://grafana.com/api/grafana/versions/stable at startup and every 24 h (pkg/services/updatemanager/grafana.go:23,60-76,95), and defaults.ini:393-398 also says grafana.com. The 10-minute ticker belongs to the plugin update check (pkg/services/updatemanager/plugins.go:106).

claim_checks.claim: docs/sources/datasources/_index.md:191-233: Grafana ships built-in core data sources including Prometheus, Loki and Tempo
claim_checks.evidence: They ship in release artifacts as catalog plugins downloaded at packaging time into data/plugins-bundled (Makefile:391-411; scripts/catalog-plugins-defaults:3-15) and are preinstalled and auto-updated at startup (pkg/setting/setting_plugins.go:35-55,201). Their source is not in this repo. Slim Docker variants omit data/plugins-bundled (Dockerfile:156-160). Elasticsearch docs say it became a standalone plugin in v13.0 (docs/sources/datasources/elasticsearch/_index.md:73). AGENTS.md:133 still lists loki as an in-tree plugin, but the directory does not exist; contribute/developer-guide.md:113-114 lists only azuremonitor and grafana-testdata-datasource.

claim_checks.claim: docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/_index.md:32-42: supported OSes are Debian/Ubuntu, RHEL/Fedora, SUSE, macOS and Windows; others are 'not recommended or supported'
claim_checks.evidence: The release matrix additionally builds linux s390x/armv6/armv7/riscv64 and windows-arm64, with riscv64 explicitly 'not an officially supported architecture' and allowed to fail (.github/workflows/release-build.yml:215-252,236). No WSL2 target or doc exists.

benchmarks.what: Minimum and 'Small' tier resources for the Grafana server process (project-documented guidance, not a measured benchmark; no benchmark runs or third-party reports were present in the working tree)
benchmarks.value: Minimum 512 MB RAM and 1 CPU core; Small tier (<25 concurrent users, <100 alert rules, <5 data sources, <200 dashboards): 2 cores, 2-4 GB RAM, 10-20 GB SSD, 1 instance

benchmarks.what: Medium and Large tier sizing guidance (project-documented; excludes data-source backends)
benchmarks.value: Medium: 4-8 cores, 8-16 GB, 2 instances. Large: 8-16+ cores, 16-32+ GB per instance, 3+ instances

benchmarks.what: Grafana Live WebSocket connection cost (project-stated estimate)
benchmarks.metric: memory per persistent connection; default connection cap
benchmarks.value: about 50 KB per connection (about 20k connections per 1 GB RAM); default cap 100 connections per server

risks: Scope gap against the stated needs: no OTLP receiver/collector, telemetry privacy filter, metrics store, logs/events store, trace/dataset/experiment store or local model server exists in this repo (see claim_checks #2). Nav entries exist only for external apps grafana-sigil-app and grafana-agento11y-app (pkg/services/navtree/navtreeimpl/applinks.go:594-595). Embedders are cloud-only vertex/bedrock/azure (pkg/storage/unified/search/embed/embedder/provider/provider.go:42-53). Assistant on-prem needs a Grafana Cloud stack (docs/sources/administration/assistant/_index.md:16-36). What is in scope is dashboards, Explore and alerting over externally provided stores.

Core data-source code is external: Prometheus, Loki, Tempo and the other listed data sources are catalog plugins downloaded from grafana.com into data/plugins-bundled at packaging time and preinstalled or auto-updated at startup (scripts/catalog-plugins-defaults:3-15; scripts/download-catalog-plugins.sh:6,146-157; pkg/setting/setting_plugins.go:35-55,201). A source-built binary lacks them until fetched (Makefile:391-411), slim Docker variants omit them (Dockerfile:156-160), and their code cannot be reviewed from this checkout.

Default-on outbound calls to grafana.com and stats.grafana.org (usage report, version check, 10-minute plugin update check, plugin preinstall and auto-update, plugin key download, news feed; see telemetry_and_network). A privacy-filtered local setup must disable them explicitly. Docs and code disagree on the version check (docs: GitHub, every ten minutes; code: grafana.com, every 24 h) (docs/sources/setup-grafana/configure-grafana/_index.md:620-621 vs pkg/services/updatemanager/grafana.go:23,63).

Insecure defaults: admin/admin initial credentials, empty http_addr (all interfaces), cookie_secure=false, a placeholder secret_key, and /metrics enabled with only optional basic auth (conf/defaults.ini:50,471-480,510,2015-2028; contribute/developer-guide.md:155-161).

Licensing: the core is AGPL-3.0-only; only the listed directories are Apache-2.0 (LICENSING.md:5-25; README.md:50). The docs recommend the Enterprise build as the default edition, with license-unlockable features. That build comes from a separate private repo that is not in this clone (docs/sources/setup-grafana/installation/debian/index.md:41; docker/index.md:30; .github/workflows/release-build.yml:91-98).

Release integrity: public workflows produce only sha256 sidecars and an SPDX SBOM; no sigstore/cosign/SLSA/provenance steps were found under .github. RPM/APT signing is done by scripts and processes outside the public workflows (scripts/build/sign_packages.sh:17-25; release-build.yml:334-340; sbom-on-release.yml:69-85). Release builds run from main or the private security mirror and dispatch an Enterprise build (release-build.yml:37-41,91-185).

Platform and build: the supported-OS list excludes WSL2 and other distros (installation/_index.md:40-42), riscv64 is explicitly unofficial (release-build.yml:236) and no GPU is used. A source build needs Go 1.26.6, Node >=22 <25 (.nvmrc v24.11.0), Yarn 4.17.1 and an 8 GB Node heap for the frontend, plus CGO/SQLite caveats (go.mod:3; package.json:12,473-476; Dockerfile:27; contribute/developer-guide.md:165-167).

Maintenance and verification: main/release CI runs against a private Enterprise overlay, and OSS-only unit/lint jobs run only for fork PRs, so main-branch results are not reproducible from this repo alone (backend-unit-tests.yml:38-42,72-125; frontend-lint.yml:40-47,60-87). The dependency surface is very large (260 direct and 398 indirect Go modules; 159 + 167 npm packages), partly mitigated by yarn enableScripts:false, npmMinimalAgeGate 3d, Renovate minimumReleaseAge 7 days, govulncheck and trufflehog (.yarnrc.yml:9,15; .github/renovate.json5:29; govulncheck.yml:40-60; trufflehog.yml:33-36). Contributor docs lag the tree (AGENTS.md:133).

checks.statement: APT repository (Debian/Ubuntu, Linux); OSS package 'grafana', Enterprise 'grafana-enterprise'. Command: sudo apt-get install -y apt-transport-https wget gnupg; sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings; sudo wget -O /etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.asc https://apt.grafana.com/gpg-full.key; sudo chmod 644 /etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.asc; echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.asc] https://apt.grafana.com stable main" | sudo tee -a /etc/apt/sources.list.d/grafana.list; sudo apt-get update; sudo apt-get install grafana
checks.note: Each step matches the doc word for word: prerequisites (:49), keyring dir, gpg-full.key download and chmod 644 (:55-57), stable repo line (:63), apt-get update (:76) and apt-get install grafana (:83). The package table (:35,37) and the Enterprise install (:90) confirm grafana / grafana-enterprise. The doc calls Enterprise 'the recommended and default edition' (:41).

LICENSE:1-2 is 'GNU AFFERO GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 19 November 2007'. The AGPL text alone doesn't choose between -only and -or-later; README.md:50, LICENSING.md:5 and package.json:3 ("license": "AGPL-3.0-only") make it -only. The Apache-2.0 directory exceptions are at LICENSING.md:9-25, and public/vendor/ keeps its upstream licenses (:27-31).

checks.field: claim_checks #2 (OTLP receiver / telemetry store / privacy filter, verified: no)
checks.statement: No OTLP receiver, telemetry store or redaction pipeline exists. OTLP code only exports Grafana's own traces (tracing.go:176-196; defaults.ini:2100-2118; tracing_file.go:29-37); there is also a download-as-OTLP helper (download.ts:110-132), and collector/pdata is used only as a data-model library (go.mod:186). The only push intake is Live /api/live/push/:streamId, which accepts InfluxDB line protocol into in-memory frames (api.go:546; push.go:48-100; convert.go:30-45). The Faro endpoint only logs and is off by default (frontend_logging.go:33-93; setting_grafana_javascript_agent.go:26).
checks.citation: pkg/infra/tracing/tracing.go:176-196; conf/defaults.ini:2100-2118; pkg/infra/tracing/tracing_file.go:29-37; public/app/features/inspector/utils/download.ts:110-132; go.mod:186; pkg/api/api.go:546; pkg/services/live/pushhttp/push.go:48-100; pkg/services/live/convert/convert.go:30-45; pkg/api/frontend_logging.go:33-93; pkg/setting/setting_grafana_javascript_agent.go:26
checks.note: Every citation matches. tracing.go:176-196 builds an otlptracegrpc client to cfg.Address. defaults.ini:2103 leaves the OTLP address empty, and :2114-2118 configure the file exporter. tracing_file.go:29-37 describes a client that writes OTLP/JSON to a file. download.ts:115-136 defaults to OTLP. go.mod:186 is collector/pdata v1.60.0, imported only by tracing_file.go and the Faro payload struct (pkg/api/frontendlogging/grafana_javascript_agent_payload.go:15-16). api.go:545-546 is commented 'POST influx line protocol'. push.go:76-97 converts the body and pushes frames to the managed stream. convert.go:30-39 accepts only the telegraf 'wide'/'labels_column' formats. frontend_logging.go:33-88 only writes to frontendLogger, and setting_grafana_javascript_agent.go:26 is enabled=MustBool(false). My own grep of pkg/, apps/, conf/, public/app and docs/sources (otlpreceiver, otlphttp, /v1/(traces|metrics|logs), Export/Register*ServiceServer) found no receiver. Its only hits were sending-side config: the image renderer's rendering_tracing_url (conf/defaults.ini:2304-2305; conf/sample.ini:2105) and a Grafana Cloud API example (otlpHttpUrl). The plugin env passthrough GF_INSTANCE_OTLP_ADDRESS (pluginconfig/envvars.go:281-285) is also sending-side. The dossier's 'show only' list leaves these out, but they don't change the 'no'.
